correctness.rationale: The map has 2337 exact fourth-iterate affine polygon cells covering unit area; 2328 have invertible I-A and nine do not. Canonicalizing solved endpoints gives 336 distinct solutions from nonsingular affine cells (including some that lie in lower-period line families); exactly 320 have least period four, forming 80 orbits. All four nontrivial singular fixed segments are period-two, with no primitive four on singular branches. Exact boundary restrictions give 23 fourth-fixed edge points already counted. Direct independent evaluation verifies all candidate points, and exact Jacobian products give cycle trace classes 32(-574), 16(578), 16(178), and 16 switching. The proof relies on full branch coverage, not on finite sampling.

value.rationale: The complete primitive-four census is a natural exact invariant of a previously studied area-preserving mixing map. The theorem distinguishes 64 regular hyperbolic cycles from 16 switching cycles while excluding the infinite two-periodic families, revealing finite-period organization in a nonuniformly hyperbolic system. It is not a tiny numerical improvement, a mere parameter restatement, or a result implied by qualitative mixing.
